## How authkit-refresh-token answers

As the loop script that pipes the token into a client,
I want exit 0 to mean "the token is on stdout" and anything else to print no token,
so that a failed mint can never feed a client a broken token.

The scenarios need the openssl CLI and the repository's tsx; AuthKit is a fake on 127.0.0.1.

**Rule: A refused mint exits 1, prints one "authkit-refresh-token:" line on stderr and no token, never echoes the refresh token, and leaves the runtime file as it was.**

### No seed: the error names the install command

Status: **verified** · Code: [`refreshAccessToken`](../src/refresh-auth.ts), [`assertAuthKitIssuer`](../src/refresh-auth.ts)

- Given the seed is missing
- Given AuthKit answers with the refresh token "rt-2"
- When I run "authkit-refresh-token sim1"

  ```console
  $ authkit-refresh-token sim1
  [stderr]
  authkit-refresh-token: no machine-user seed or runtime record for 'sim1' (looked at ~/.config/spellkave/sim-players/sim1.json and ~/.config/spellkave/player-mcp/machine-user-sim1.seed.json). Install it: scripts/sim/install-machine-seed.sh --player sim1
  [exit 1]
  ```

- Then authkit-refresh-token exits with 1
- Then stdout is empty, and stderr is one line that says "scripts/sim/install-machine-seed.sh --player sim1"
- Then stderr does not contain "rt-seed"
- Then AuthKit received 0 requests
- Then there is no runtime file

## Mint an access token for a simulated player

As an operator who runs simulated players, or the loop script that mints their tokens,
I want one command that turns a player's installed seed into a fresh AuthKit access token,
so that the player signs in as the same world identity as an interactive login.

AuthKit rotates the refresh token on every use, so the command keeps the live one in a
runtime file and never writes back to the provisioned seed. The
scenarios need the openssl CLI and the repository's tsx; AuthKit is a fake on 127.0.0.1.

### A seeded player gets a token, and the rotated refresh token goes to the runtime file

Status: **verified** · Code: [`authkit-refresh-token.ts`](../src/bin/authkit-refresh-token.ts), [`mintMachineAccessToken`](../src/refresh-auth.ts)

> The grant goes to the AuthKit-domain endpoint with the MCP resource, so iss, aud and sub match an interactive login. `authkit-refresh-token sim1 > token` is safe: stdout holds only the token. The rotated refresh token goes to the runtime file ~/.config/spellkave/sim-players/<player>.json (mode 0600); the seed stays as installed.

- Given the seed holds the refresh token "rt-seed"
- Given AuthKit answers with the refresh token "rt-2"
- When I run "authkit-refresh-token sim1"

  <details><summary>authkit-refresh-token sim1</summary>

  ```console
  $ authkit-refresh-token sim1
  <access token from AuthKit>
  [exit 0]
  ```

  </details>

- Then authkit-refresh-token succeeds
- Then stdout is the access token AuthKit issued, and stderr is empty
- Then AuthKit's last request was a refresh grant spending "rt-seed"
- Then the runtime file holds the refresh token "rt-2", readable only by me
- Then the seed still holds the refresh token "rt-seed"

### The next run spends the rotated token, not the seed

Status: **verified** · Code: [`readRecordFile`](../src/refresh-auth.ts)

> Once the runtime file exists it wins over the seed, so AuthKit's rotation chain continues.

- Given the seed holds the refresh token "rt-seed"
- Given AuthKit answers with the refresh token "rt-2"
- Given I ran "authkit-refresh-token sim1" once
- Given AuthKit answers with the refresh token "rt-3"
- When I run "authkit-refresh-token sim1"

  <details><summary>authkit-refresh-token sim1</summary>

  ```console
  $ authkit-refresh-token sim1
  <access token from AuthKit>
  [exit 0]
  ```

  </details>

- Then authkit-refresh-token succeeds
- Then AuthKit's last request was a refresh grant spending "rt-2"
- Then the runtime file holds the refresh token "rt-3", readable only by me
